scenes.heading: Angles of elevation and depression
scenes.sub: Look up, look down, find the height
scenes.say: How tall is that tower? How far away is that boat? You can’t reach them with a tape measure, but you can measure an angle with your eyes and let trigonometry do the rest.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Tilt your chin up to see a bird, down to see your shoes
scenes.science: Elevation is up from horizontal; depression is down from it
scenes.breaks: Your eyes are about 1.5 m above the ground, so you may need to add your eye height.
scenes.say: Look straight ahead. That’s the horizontal. Tilt your chin up to see a bird: that’s an angle of elevation. Tilt it down to see your shoes: that’s an angle of depression. Both start from looking straight ahead. Just remember your eyes are above the ground.

scenes.heading: Angle of elevation
scenes.say: First the ground and the tree. Then the dashed line of sight from the observer up to the top, at thirty-eight degrees. The height is opposite and thirty metres is adjacent, so tan thirty-eight equals h over thirty. H is about twenty-three point four metres.
scenes.caption: tan 38° = h/30, so h = 30 tan 38° ≈ 23.4 m.

scenes.heading: Angle of depression
notes: Alternate angles: 24° at the boat too
scenes.say: Now a forty-five metre cliff. Draw a dashed horizontal from the top, then the line of sight down to the boat. The angle of depression is twenty-four degrees. The horizontal and the ground are parallel, so the same twenty-four degrees appears at the boat. So d equals forty-five divided by tan twenty-four, about one hundred and one point one metres.
scenes.caption: Alternate angles: 24° at the boat too. d = 45 ÷ tan 24° ≈ 101.1 m.

scenes.heading: Don’t forget eye height
scenes.question: Eyes 1.6 m up, 25 m from a building, elevation 52°. How tall is the building?
scenes.say: Mia’s eyes are one point six metres up. Above her eyes, the building rises twenty-five times tan fifty-two, about thirty-two metres. Then add her eye height. The building is about thirty-three point six metres tall.

scenes.heading: Two observers, one height
scenes.say: When the same tower is seen from two points in a line, write each distance as h divided by tan of the angle. Subtract them to get the gap between the two points. That gives one equation, and you solve it for h.

points: Both angles start at the horizontal
Draw the horizontal, vertical, line of sight
Add eye height at the end
scenes.say: Quick recap. Elevation and depression are both measured from the horizontal. The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation, by alternate angles. Draw the triangle, use soh cah toa, and add any eye height at the end. Now try the practice questions!
